meta.title: DSH Dispatch Console
meta.description: Dispatch and monitor AI CLI headless processes in Harness (four engines: ZCode / OpenCode / Qoder / WorkBuddy): single-writer lock, usage and context, concurrency and fallback chain, WorkBuddy sign-in

ui.title: Dispatch Console
ui.headerTip: Open or hide the dispatch panel
ui.noFileLocks: (no file locks: jobs did not declare write, using whole-repo lock)
ui.chanThinkingHint: Channel default thinking: Agent decides = the dispatching agent picks a concrete level per task; a concrete level is a hard rule for dispatched agents (dispatches without an explicit level follow it; new sessions only)
ui.thinkingStaleHint: This level is not in the current model declaration (the model level table may have changed) — dispatch would be rejected by the runner; pick a valid level
ui.jobClearHint: Clear every job in this tab (removed from the list and persisted to dismissed.json; running jobs cannot be cleared)
ui.rerunTitle: Re-send the original prompt in the same session (--resume; without a sessionId it hands off)
ui.continueTitle: Send a NEW instruction into the same session (--resume + new prompt)
ui.continueNoSession: This task has no sessionId, so it cannot be continued (use Rerun to hand off instead)
ui.emptyOffline: Host not connected: no process data (live data needs the Remote wiring)
ui.localNote: Local usage (verifiable): ledger-aggregated 5h / week / today windows
ui.engineWeekUsed: Engine week used (engine-local DB total, not plan usage)
ui.planQuotaPending: Plan quota remaining: not wired — no such method on the CLI RPC surface (app-server usage/stats is local-used only); defer to the ZCode client
ui.engModelOnly: Models are probed from this channel
ui.chanEngineHintZcode: ZCode engine: supports mode (build/edit/plan/yolo) and memoryBench; thinking maps to ZCode reasoning-level.
ui.chanEngineHintOpencode: OpenCode engine: no mode / memoryBench (never passed); thinking maps to OpenCode --variant; --auto is never added by default (the sub-agent will not auto-approve permissions) — to allow it, the dispatcher must pass auto=true explicitly, and the job row then shows an "auto-approved" badge; the free tier is IP rate-limited and every call spins up a temporary server (slow cold start), so its concurrency cap is separate and lower (default 2).
ui.filtAvailableHint: List only channels that are currently usable (off = also list unusable channels with their reason)
ui.filtFreeHint: List only channels that need no paid quota: the free tier (Start Plan) and OpenCode free models; personal keys and paid plan channels are hidden
ui.filtHint: Filters: Available only (on by default; turn off to also see unusable channels) | Free only (off by default; turn on to keep only the free tier and OpenCode free models). They only change what these two dropdowns list — they never change the current selection.
ui.chanLoading: Loading channel list… (host just started or first probe in flight; failures retry automatically, no refresh needed)
ui.chanEngineHintQoder: Qoder engine: no mode / memoryBench; thinking maps to Qoder --reasoning-effort. In headless mode any operation that would ask for confirmation is denied outright, so the executor defaults to --permission-mode accept_edits (it can edit files inside the working directory; shell stays gated). To allow everything the dispatcher must pass auto=true explicitly (mapped to bypass_permissions). Note: non-default permission modes only apply inside trusted directories — an untrusted directory falls back to default and write operations are denied *very quietly* (the task reports success but nothing changed), so the executor compares init.permissionMode and warns loudly on fallback. Usage is reported via total_credits (this engine's token fields may be 0).
ui.enginesHint: Execution engines auto-detected on this machine (form / version / login). The plugin searches in five levels — env var → config → PATH → known install locations (incl. other drives) — so no path needs to be filled in by hand.
ui.autoApprovedHint: This job explicitly enabled OpenCode --auto: all permissions not explicitly denied were allowed (off by default; only takes effect when the caller sets it explicitly)
ui.jobStalledHint: No runner heartbeat/output for over 150s: it may be stuck on an upstream request, MCP connect or a lock. Kill and re-dispatch, or use action=tail for the last output.
ui.chanOfflineHint: Host not connected: channel/model come from the host Remote face and unlock once connected
ui.timedOutWatchdog: watchdog kill (still running after timeoutMin+120s grace)
ui.handoffConfirm: Channel switch = handoff rerun: a new session starts and the unfinished part is handed over
ui.fallbackEnableTitle: Auto fallback: click to enable/disable. When enabled, quota-exhausted / not-entitled / signing-required pauses hand off to the target chosen below (downstream quota is consumed)
ui.fallbackHint: Same option logic as the Channels section above: empty model = that channel's default model; "Agent decides" resolves via ZCode's default rule. New sessions only.
ui.fallbackOfflineHint: Host not connected: fallback settings live in the host work dir and unlock once connected
ui.switchTitle: Dispatch master switch: click to toggle (writes collab/dispatch.switch.json, effective for all sessions)
ui.switchHintOffline: Host not connected: run dispatch-switch.mjs in a terminal to toggle
ui.switchOffBlocked: Dispatch master switch is off: all dispatch entries are rejected; re-enable via the title-bar switch or dispatch-switch.mjs
ui.seqHint: Selecting "Sequential dispatch" in "Model" IS the switch (there is no separate toggle): the list below is tried top to bottom, an error moves on to the next entry (quota exhausted / rate-limited pauses count too), and it only reports failure after the whole list is exhausted — auto fallback runs after that. The main channel and the fallback target are independent: an empty model on the main channel uses the main engine's list; otherwise an empty model on the fallback target uses the fallback engine's list (lists are stored per engine). The list applies to the engine currently shown (ZCode / OpenCode / Qoder each have their own). The "Effort" dropdown on each row sets that model's own thinking level ("Default" = the engine default) — the global effort setting is locked in sequential mode because models differ in supported levels. Note: switching models starts a NEW session; file changes already made are kept and the model is told to continue.
ui.seqHintShort: Sequential dispatch: no model pinned, so an error switches to the next model down the list (main channel and fallback target each keep their own list)
ui.seqEmpty: (No selectable models for this engine; an empty list means sequential dispatch has no effect)
ui.seqOfflineHint: Host not connected: the sequential order lives in the host work dir and unlocks once connected
ui.seqHintCard: Tries the list below top to bottom: an error moves on to the next entry; switching models starts a NEW session
ui.seqUseMain: The main channel is using this list
ui.seqUseFallback: The fallback target is using this list
ui.seqUseBoth: Both the main channel and the fallback target use this list
ui.seqUseNone: Not active yet: pick "Sequential dispatch" in Model to try this list
ui.tvTailHint: Use action=tail to read the output
ui.splitEnableTitle: When on: as the main channel nears its limit, new tasks are auto-routed to the fallback channel (the two channels' slots add up ⇒ more concurrency)
ui.splitNeedDistinctHint: Set the Auto-fallback target to a channel **different** from the main one first (same channel = same slots, splitting is pointless)
ui.splitHint: Splitting applies only when no channel was explicitly given (explicit ⇒ your choice is respected); split tasks carry splitFrom for verification; if the target is also full, tasks queue honestly instead of being forced in.
ui.chanEngineHintCodebuddy: WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy engine (runs the **official CLI**; no reverse proxy involved): no mode / memoryBench; thinking maps to CodeBuddy --effort (the level set is declared by the CLI itself in --help: minimal→max, 6 levels). The executor defaults to --permission-mode acceptEdits (can edit files inside the working directory); to allow everything the dispatcher must pass auto=true explicitly (mapped to bypassPermissions). Note: the CLI login is **independent of the WorkBuddy desktop app** — the desktop can be signed in while headless runs still report "Authentication required"; the job then pauses as `not logged in` and you need to start the CLI interactively once and run /login. This CLI exits with code 0 even when the task fails, and the executor folds that into the done exit code — so do not judge success from exit=0 alone.
ui.wbStateResidueHint: ⚠ This is the most common cause of "I signed in but it keeps saying not signed in": a forced kill (taskkill /F) left a .logged-out marker, and the credential file is ignored while it exists. Click Sign in once to renew (it removes the marker automatically), or rename that marker file as a backup and retry (no re-sign-in needed).
ui.wbLoginHint: Starts a local sign-in service from the official WorkBuddy CLI (codebuddy --serve) and returns a **sign-in link**. Note: /login is a slash command inside the CLI UI — typing it in PowerShell fails with "not recognized"; CLI sign-in is **independent of the desktop app**. This plugin never reads or writes credentials; it only drives the official process.
ui.wbLoginStopHint: Stop the sign-in service (also ends the CLI child process)
ui.wbLoginTimeout: sign-in request timed out (host did not respond within 45s)
ui.wbLoginNoMethod: host does not expose login() — restart DSH and retry (happens when the client is newer than the host)
